extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent applicants, patent attorneys, and pro se filers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and examiner guidance for the content, form, and submission of the patent specification and related materials under MPEP §608 and implementing regulations (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112(a), 37 CFR 1.71, 1.52, 1.58). Covers adequacy of disclosure, paper/format rules, electronic submissions (sequence listings, large tables), and related examiner form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate disclosure (35 U.S.C. 112(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application as filed must contain a full and clear disclosure of the invention in the manner prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a). All amendments and claims must find descriptive basis in the original disclosure; no new matter may be introduced after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adequate disclosure requirement ensures the public receives something in return for patent rights. Applicant may rely on the specification with original claims and drawings as filed. See also 37 CFR 1.121(f) and MPEP § 608.04. If the application obviously fails to disclose with the clarity required by 35 U.S.C. 112, require revision (see MPEP § 702.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to offensive language or drawings (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner notes language or drawings that could be deemed offensive to any race, religion, sex, ethnic group, or nationality, object as failing to comply with 37 CFR 1.3 (lack of decorum and courtesy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such language/drawings should be deleted or propriety resolved before publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) or before passing application to issue. See MPEP § 714.25 for amendments/papers presented in violation of 37 CFR 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description and enablement (37 CFR 1.71(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the disclosure enables the invention across its full scope; vagueness, verbosity, or unclear terms may lead to objection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a). Use form paragraphs (e.g., 6.30) when the specification is replete with unclear terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must set forth the precise invention (37 CFR 1.71(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must set forth the precise invention for which a patent is solicited in such manner as to distinguish it from other inventions and from what is old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe completely a specific embodiment of the invention (process, machine, manufacture, composition) and explain mode of operation or principle when applicable. Best mode contemplated by the inventor must be set forth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of improvements (37 CFR 1.71(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an improvement, the specification must particularly point out the part(s) of the process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter to which the improvement relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confine the description to the specific improvement and any cooperating parts necessary for complete understanding or description of the improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement (37 CFR 1.71(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The best mode contemplated by the inventor of carrying out the invention must be set forth in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include disclosure of the inventor's best-known way of practicing the invention at filing; omission may be objectionable under statutes/regulations in force at filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/mask work notice and required authorization paragraph (37 CFR 1.71(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed in an application adjacent to copyright/mask work material, but must be limited to elements provided by law and must be accompanied by a specific authorization statement in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the exact authorization paragraph as set forth in the regulation at the beginning (preferably first paragraph) of the specification if including a copyright/mask work notice. See examples in §1.71(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must commence on separate sheet; section separation (37 CFR 1.71(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must commence on a separate sheet, and each sheet including part of the specification may not include other parts of the application (claims, abstract, Sequence Listing). Claims, abstract, and Sequence Listing should each begin on a new page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sections are separately indexed in the Image File Wrapper (IFW); avoid overlap of sections on a single page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names of joint research agreement parties (37 CFR 1.71(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification may disclose or be amended to disclose names of parties to a joint research agreement; such amendments may require a processing fee if not filed within specified time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow timing windows (e.g., within three months of filing or before first Office action on the merits) and include fee per §1.17(i). If added after issue fee paid, correction may require certificate of correction (35 U.S.C. 255 and §1.323).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification never returned; retain accurate copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification is never returned to applicant; applicants should retain an accurate copy and must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 when amending the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys/applicants should keep their own complete copies of the filed specification; follow amendment procedures per MPEP §714 and 37 CFR 1.121.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance of British English spellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not object merely because applicants use British English spellings rather than American English; 37 CFR 1.52(b)(1)(ii) requires English, not specifically American English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No need to require replacement of British spellings (e.g., 'colour') with American equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.29 — Disclosure objected to, minor informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.29 to object to minor informalities in the disclosure (e.g., spelling errors, inconsistent terminology, numbering of elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out the informalities requiring correction; see form paragraphs 6.28–6.31 for specific informalities. Use when defects are minor and easily correctable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.29 — Specification spacing of lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Require new application papers with lines 1 1/2 or double spaced on good quality paper where spacing makes reading difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when line spacing of the specification makes reading difficult; reference 37 CFR 1.52(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.30 — Numerous errors in specification (35 U.S.C. 112(a) noncompliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification is replete with terms which are not clear, concise, and exact, require revision to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the specification contains numerous unclear, inexact, or verbose terms; request applicant to revise carefully to meet statutory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper requirements — physical paper characteristics (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers to become part of the permanent USPTO records must be on sheets of specified sizes (A4 or 8.5x11), white, flexible, unbound, single-sided, with specified margins (top ≥2.0 cm, left ≥2.5 cm, right ≥2.0 cm, bottom ≥2.0 cm), durable and non-shiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers must be legible for photographic/electronic reproduction. Avoid holes in sheets. Pre-printed Office forms and certain reissue formats are excluded. Electronic submissions must meet patent electronic filing system requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement and translations (37 CFR 1.52(b)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application papers must be in English or accompanied by an English translation with a statement of accuracy and required processing fee (for nonprovisional applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonprovisional applications filed in a language other than English require an English translation and fee per §1.17(i) or risk abandonment; provisional applications have different rules (no translation required at provisional stage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of specification text (line spacing, font, single-column) (37 CFR 1.52(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification (other than reissue/reexam) must have 1 1/2 or double spacing, text in a nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier, preferably font size 12; captial letters at least 0.3175 cm high; may be no smaller than 0.21 cm), and only a single column of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims, abstract, and Sequence Listing have separate page rules. Paragraph numbering recommended in the [0001] format and placement; nontext elements are part of the surrounding paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and abstract separate page requirements (37 CFR 1.52(b)(3)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must commence on a separate physical sheet/electronic page; abstract must commence on a separate sheet or be first page in certain proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims and abstract are not combined on same page with other sections to allow proper indexing and IFW separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and paragraph numbering rules (37 CFR 1.52(b)(5)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages of the specification (including claims and abstract) must be consecutively numbered starting with 1, with numbers centrally located above or preferably below the text. Paragraphs (other than claims/abstract) may be individually numbered using Arabic numerals with at least four numerals enclosed in square brackets (e.g., [0001]) and highlighted in bold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph numbers should appear to the right of the left margin as the first item in each paragraph and be followed by a gap. Nontext elements and lists are considered part of the surrounding paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlineation and substitute specification (37 CFR 1.52(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlineation, erasure, cancellation, or other alteration may be made before or after signing of the inventor's oath/declaration provided statements in oath/declaration remain applicable; a substitute specification (§1.125) may be required if papers do not comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes are extensive or noncompliant, require substitute specification; follow amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc submissions — permitted content and format (37 CFR 1.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain documents (Computer Program Listing Appendix, Sequence Listing, Large Tables) may be submitted on a read-only optical disc in compliance with specified requirements (ISO 9660, ASCII/plain text or XML as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discs must be PC/Mac compatible, contain ASCII plain text (or XML for Sequence Listing XML), be enclosed in hard case, accompanied by a transmittal letter with specified metadata (inventor name, title, docket, application number, OS, file names/sizes/dates), and bear a permanent label with specified info. Unreadable files are treated as not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-only optical disc labeling and duplicate copies (37 CFR 1.52(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must have a permanent label with inventor, title, docket, application number/filing date (if known), date recorded, and disc order; duplicates are required for Large Tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two discs required for Large Tables so OPAP can retain a copy and provide one for examiners. In duplicate-submission cases, if discs differ, Office uses 'Copy 1'. Replacement discs for amendments must be labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee determination for electronic/read-only submissions (37 CFR 1.52(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules to determine application size fees: for read-only discs, each 3 KB counts as a sheet; for electronic filing system, paper size equivalent is 75% of number of sheets when rendered by the system. Exclusions apply for Sequence Listings and Computer Program Listing Appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversized electronic sequence listing submissions may incur additional fees per §1.21(o). See specific exclusion lists in paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical and mathematical formula/tables formatting and 'Large Tables' rules (37 CFR 1.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical and mathematical formulas and tables must comply with 1.52(a)/(b), may be placed landscape if needed, require block (nonscript) fonts with specified minimum sizes and spacing. 'Large Tables' (individual table >50 pages or total tables >100 pages) may be submitted in ASCII plain text electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large Tables submitted as ASCII must maintain spatial relationships (alignment) and meet compatibility requirements. Tables should be closely spaced consistent with legibility. See paragraph (c)-(d) for details and electronic submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of lengthy tables in published documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Lengthy tables (e.g., more than 200 consecutive pages or large numbers of tables) submitted electronically will not be published as part of the patent document but published separately on the USPTO website with a standardized 'LENGTHY TABLE' statement inserted in the patent/patent application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tables are separately published, the patent document contains a single-column statement directing readers to the USPTO website for the table and advising of fee-based availability upon request. Applicants may submit lengthy tables in electronic form to avoid costly printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.63.01 — Table <51 pages submitted only as text file
rubrics_metrics.description: If a descriptive table of less than 51 pages is submitted only in ASCII text format electronically, applicant is required to cancel references to the table, file a paper or PDF version in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52, and change references accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whenever a table on read-only optical disc or text-file via electronic filing is less than 51 pages and was filed on/after Sept 8, 2000. Examiner inserts page range of references in the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.63.02 — Table column/row relationship not maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Tables submitted as ASCII text must maintain spatial relationships; if data are misaligned and cannot be accurately read, require replacement text file with proper alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert bracketed area of misalignment in form paragraph; used whenever table data cannot be accurately read due to misalignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing submissions rules (MPEP §608.05(c), 37 CFR 1.821/1.831)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications disclosing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences must provide a sequence listing: for applications filed before July 1, 2022, a Sequence Listing as ASCII plain text per 37 CFR 1.821–1.824; for applications filed on/after July 1, 2022, a Sequence Listing XML per 37 CFR 1.831–1.834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings must be submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or on read-only optical disc as required. See MPEP §§ 2412–2419 (post-2022) and §§ 2420 et seq. (pre-2022) for detailed technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission handling — unreadable files treated as not submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file submitted on read-only optical disc or electronically is unreadable, it is treated as not having been submitted and the Office will issue a notice requiring compliant submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should verify readability and conformity to format rules; disc/transmittal metadata requirements must be followed to avoid processing delays or abandonment.
